import subprocess
import threading


def worker(argv):
    subprocess.run(argv)


argv = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-timer-run"]
t = threading.Timer(1, worker, args=(argv,))
t.run()
rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, static only, nothing executed. threading.Timer(interval, function, args, kwargs) binds self.function=worker, self.args=(argv,), self.kwargs={} at construction (threading.py:1370-1376) and creates self.finished=Event() unset. t.run() is an ordinary method call on the stored object; Timer.run executes self.finished.wait(self.interval) and then, because finished is still unset, self.function(*self.args, **self.kwargs) synchronously in the calling thread (threading.py:1382-1386). No new thread is ever created because start() is never called, and finished can never be set because t has no other reference and cancel() (the only pre-run setter, threading.py:1378-1380) is unreachable; the interval length does not change which call is made. argv is a module-scope literal list bound before construction and never rebound, so the single statically determined effect is subprocess.run(["pacman","-S","r22-timer-run"]) in the caller, serialized by shlex.join as 'pacman -S r22-timer-run' -> one observed host_mutation row, zero eval_unparsed/unparsed_spawns.
